item.title: CKB Talk Daily Brief - 2026-10-09
item.description: ## 今日发生了什么 今天 Nervos Talk 上最集中的讨论是 ArthurZhang 围绕“在 CKB 上构建 Based EVM 层”连续补充多种架构选项，并延伸到 Myelin 的排序与安全模型 [S05, S06, S08, S09, S10]。与此同时，生态双周报 #26 发布，Waymark 钱包恢复新帖出现，Twine 的 Fiber P2P PoC 也有更新 [S01, S03, S04]。DAO 相关讨论同样活跃，涉及 DAO Treasury 激活、DAO Cycle Alerts 和 CKAutomata 支付自动化 [S02, S11, S14]。 ## 重点话题 ArthurZhang 在同一帖子中连续展开 Option 1 Based ZK Rollup、Option 2 CKB-Based EVM Validium、Option 3 Based Optimistic EVM Rollup with CKB-VM Court，并把 Option 4 外部 DA 方案列为暂搁置 [S05, S06, S08, S09]。他随后把三种方案放在一起比较，提出“一个排序协议、三种安全模型”，并列出以太坊先例与 Myelin 的开放问题 [S10]。中间还讨论了 sequencing tip contention 等三个协议挑战 [S07]。 CKB Ecosystem Biweekly Update #26 发布，回顾过去两周关键开发与生态进展，并提到 @CKBdev 于 9 月 17 日发布 CKB v0.210.0 [S03]。...

item.title: Twine: Buy and Sell CKB Without Depositing on an Exchange (Fiber P2P PoC) (1 posts)
item.description: The last reply described the proof of concept: a Flutter app and a Rust daemon on one machine, an HTTP API, a mock Fiber node in the tests, and a solver who was trusting a picture. item.title: Waymark — Recovering useful wallet state without starting from zero (1 posts)
item.description: Hi everyone, I’ve been testing a recovery problem around CKB light-client wallets. When you restore a wallet with your seed phrase, you get control of your wallet again. But the wallet may still have to rebuild a lot of the local information it had already gathered before — account discovery, transaction history, live Cells, sync progress, light-client state, and other data it needs to become fully useful again. I wanted to see if that part could also be recovered safely. That became Waymark. GitHub: github.com GitHub - Ticoworld/waymark Contribute to Ticoworld/waymark development by creating an account on GitHub. The idea Waymark separates two things that normally get treated as one...

item.title: Towards a Based EVM Layer on CKB: Three Architectural Options with Myelin (6 posts)
item.description: Option 1: A Based ZK Rollup on CKB When discussing an EVM environment on CKB, the conversation usually begins with execution: Solidity compatibility, Ethereum RPCs and the migration of existing DeFi protocols. Yet execution may no longer be the defining question. Mature EVM implementations already exist. The harder questions concern who orders the next batch, what CKB itself ought to verify, and how users retain control over their assets when execution takes place elsewhere. I have been exploring whether Myelin could provide the off-chain foundation for a based EVM architecture whose canonical ordering and settlement are governed by CKB itself. item.title: Introducing Myelin: a CKB-aligned off-chain Cell session runtime (1 posts)
item.description: Hi @jm9k, thanks — interesting question. In principle, yes, but I would distinguish extending the off-chain Cell model from changing CKB’s underlying consensus rules. Myelin already supports additional session-level semantics, such as typed-cell constraints, logical conflict scheduling and state commitments, without changing the underlying CKB transaction format. For a proposed “Cell Model v1.5”, I see two possibilities: Compatible extensions: Richer transaction abstractions or validation policies that can be lowered to CKB-compatible CellTx operations. These can preserve Myelin’s existing isomorphic execution model, provided the relevant rules remain verifiable under CkbStrict....

item.title: Introducing CKAutomata: Payment Automation and Nervos DAO Harvest on CKB (1 posts)
item.description: Hello everyone, I have been working on CKAutomata, a payment automation application built for CKB. The idea is simple: you choose what a payment should do and when it should happen. Your wallet shows you the complete plan before you approve it. CKAutomata then watches the chain and submits only the payment you approved when the right time arrives. The main feature is Nervos DAO Harvest. It helps a user collect earned DAO compensation and put the original CKB amount back into a new DAO deposit without having to remember each withdrawal step.
